newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Missoni basks in languid tropical luxury.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Missoni basks in languid tropical luxury.

text.p: Italian fashion house Missoni evoked luxuriously hot tropics and cooling splashes of sea water in its rainbow display of women's ready-to-wear styles on Thursday.

Calling the spring/summer 1997 collection "Water Follies", Missoni cited sunsets and rain forests as the inspiration behind the cocktail of violet, aquamarine, red and ochre laid side by side in zig-zag wave patterns and irregular diagonal stripes.

Hems brushed ankles or skimmed the floor giving an elegant and fluid silhouette and exuding an air of languid, comfortable sophistication, rendered more casual for beachwear when models padded down the catwalk barefoot.

For evening, models wore sequinned full length gowns or tunics and camisole tops and trousers in violet, red and yellow horizontal stripes, some tied at the waist, others low backed, as well as similar styles solely in purple or pink.
Missoni said water was the centre of the collection, with fluidity and freshness conveyed using "liquid" fabrics like viscose and glittering or shiny materials.

Daywear included straight wraparound skirts, long shifts, towelling tops and a bobbled "baby bird" material in the same tropical colours for a strapless bikini and bathing suit, while footwear was either high-heeled elegance or simple flat sandals.

Designer Krizia also took a casually sophisticated approach with her wide-ranging collection late on Wednesday, aiming at extremes in length. Trousers and skirts either fell to mid-calf or the ankle, or else were cut high to the top of the thigh.

For daywear, wide, straightlegged black or crisp white linen trousers stopping short of the ankle were matched with flat sandals, mud coloured linen jackets and pristine white shirts while other pants included generous dungarees and dungaree shorts as well as wide waisted baggies held up by braces.
Innovations included brief sleeveless tops stopping short of the waist but held in place by thin material straps wound round the bare midriff.
Crisp white Indian-style tunics fell straight to the calf with separate panels swinging freely over narrow white leggings.

Stripes featured with orange diagonals smudged at the edge as if the dye were bleeding into a cream background, while Krizia also displayed a series of dresses, skirts and trousers with rich orange deepening to red and then to purple.

For evening, pastel organza and chiffon in pale pink and yellow overlaid each other for classic shaped ball gowns, giving a full skirted effect against a petite shoulderless or subtle shouldered bodice.
Then, for the slinkier silhouette came sequinned glamour in the shape of full length delicate salmon pink sheathes.
Italian style guru Giorgio Armani unveils his second line Emporio Armani collection later on Thursday while luxury fashion house Gucci parades its line-up in the evening.
The eight-day shows run until Sunday, with Armani closing the displays with his main Giorgio Armani label.
